original_test_intent: Inject the specified 1.8V LDO PowerGood fault or transition on each required PMIC, verify the approved correctable/fatal semantics and exact PGOOD behavior, then prove the 1.8V output and its dependent PMIC functions recover without memory impact.
original_method: Identify the physical 1.8V LDO and PGOOD bit/polarity per PMIC; prove railtype9 and parameter meanings; map DIMM/PMIC/I2C targets; baseline 1.8V, PGOOD and dependent functions; inject one tuple with synchronized measurement; correlate fresh status/log evidence; measure deassert/assert timing and reset/no-reset; clear/restore and validate memory before another target.
manual_activity: The PMIC/power owner defines the railtype9 stimulus and PGOOD polarity, maps each physical target, monitors one injection and restores 1.8V, PGOOD, bus and memory state.
required_inputs: PMIC proof railtype9 selects Vout_1.8V LDO PowerGood and definitions of voltagetype0/1
Fault polarity and expected PGOOD deassert/assert, correctable/fatal severity and reset/no-reset behavior
Per-DIMM/PMIC socket/die/UMC/channel/slot/dimm, LDO dependency and PMIC part/address map
Wistron BMC/platform I2C controller/bus/address/OOB path and PGOOD/status register response
Command continuation plus full target matrix
1.8V tolerance, PGOOD timing, dependent-function/memory limits, fresh PMIC/CPER/SEL evidence, timeout and restoration
safety_requirements: Dedicated instrumented SUT with independent OOB and calibrated 1.8V/PGOOD monitoring
Confirm target PMIC/LDO and dependent functions before injection
One target/parameter once; abort on unsafe voltage, unexpected PGOOD polarity/reset, bus loss, DIMM/MCA error or missing evidence
Preserve status before approved clear and verify stable 1.8V/PGOOD reassertion
No automatic target loop; restore PMIC mode/recovery, SPD ownership, telemetry, I2C and HDT
agent_execution_scope: Validate LDO/PGOOD identity, polarity, severity, target/I2C matrix, timing and recovery plan
Collect read-only 1.8V/PGOOD telemetry, raw status, exact timeline, PMIC/CPER/SEL, dependencies and memory health
Do not infer polarity/target, modify PMIC/I2C/BIOS/HDT, inject, reset, clear, repeat, recover or decide verdict
engineer_actions: Resolve severity/polarity and approve target matrix
Approve voltage/PGOOD timing and dependent-health oracle
Restore state and issue per-target verdict

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Generic PMIC/power-good logs cannot prove the 1.8V LDO voltage, PGOOD polarity, transition time or physical target.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: After railtype9 and PGOOD semantics are approved, run one mapped tuple with synchronized 1.8V/PGOOD capture, correlate target-specific evidence, then prove electrical, dependent-function and memory recovery.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: listvalidumc, 0:0:3, railtype9, voltagetype0/1, dimm0, Fatal label, correctable Criteria, all-DIMM scope, PMIC/I2C settings and 360/120-minute values remain preserved as disputed inputs.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Execute one instrumented 1.8V LDO PGOOD transition per PMIC with exact polarity/timing, target evidence and controlled reassertion.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds fault polarity, electrical range, timing, I2C mapping, dependent-function checks, reset policy and explicit restoration.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Tool PASS and a log line cannot prove the 1.8V output or PGOOD signal changed and recovered as intended.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Dropping the LDO may remove PMIC logic or telemetry, making in-band evidence incomplete and recovery uncertain.

project_override_considerations: Use independent measurement when the PMIC/I2C interface may lose power with the LDO. I2C access remains BMC/platform-management scope and must not be inferred from host enumeration.
expected_evidence: Railtype9/parameter/polarity specification and physical 1.8V LDO/PGOOD/PMIC/DIMM/I2C topology
Pinned tool/spec with calibrated 1.8V, PGOOD and raw status baseline
Exact injection with synchronized voltage/PGOOD/event timeline and approved reset/no-reset outcome
Fresh target-specific PMIC/CPER/SEL evidence, including status captured independently if I2C drops
Stable 1.8V and PGOOD reassertion, dependent PMIC functions, DIMM enumeration and clean memory health

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Procedure says Fatal while Criteria says correctable, and the title does not state whether PGOOD is forced low, high or faulted. All DIMMs/voltage types are requested from a fixed tuple; railtype9/parameter semantics, command continuation, electrical range and timing are undefined.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The 1.8V LDO PowerGood target and seed tuple are identifiable. Engineering can define polarity and safe electrical acceptance, so static review completes.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Reliability row 97 Wistron-System RAS-00817-V002: prove railtype9 targets Vout_1.8V LDO PowerGood and define voltagetype0/1 plus PGOOD fault polarity; reconcile Fatal label with correctable Criteria and reset/no-reset behavior; map every DIMM/PMIC/LDO/dependency and Wistron BMC/platform I2C controller/bus/address/OOB path; approve command/tuple matrix, 1.8V tolerance and PGOOD timing, PMIC/CPER/SEL evidence, dependent-function/memory recovery, aborts and restoration.

review_improvement: Adds actual 1.8V and PGOOD polarity/timing evidence and accounts for loss of the PMIC interface itself during the fault.
independent_technical_reasoning: PowerGood is a signal with polarity and timing, not merely a log category. If the injected fault removes the PMIC's 1.8V logic supply, the I2C evidence path may disappear, so independent electrical capture is required. The source's Fatal label and correctable Criteria cannot determine whether reset is acceptable, and every PMIC needs its own physical mapping and recovery proof.
